To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

salivary cortisol concentration in response to ACTH is repeatable in healthy horses in the short- (2 wk) and long-term (5 mo) and that the Freiberger horses show a lower salivary cortisol increase after ACTH administration than Warmblood horses.
the salivary cortisol concentrations in healthy horses increase after ACTH stimulation and the test is repeatably in the short- but not in the long-term.
the administration of 1 μg/kg ACTH in healthy adult horses reliably stimulates the secretion of cortisol in saliva and that the test can be repeated in the short-term but not in the long-term.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a non-invasive test that is repeatable and easy to perform in horses.
the development of the ACTH test as a useful tool for the diagnosis of equine pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction.
the development of a test that is repeatable, easy to perform and that is minimally invasive for the horse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ACTH stimulation tests in horses can be repeated at short and long term intervals and that the test is reliable.
the test is a useful tool to evaluate the adrenal cortex function in the short-term.
the ACTH stimulation tests in healthy horses are repeatable in the long-term and not in the short-term, and the results are influenced by breed and sex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ACTH stimulation is repeatable in healthy horses in short-term and long-term, however the test results are not comparable between horses.
the test can be used to compare horses within the same group, but not between groups.
the salivary cortisol ACTH stimulation test is a reliable and repeatable test to assess the adrenal capacity to secrete cortisol in horses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ACTH stimulation tests are not interchangeable and that the same test has to be repeated if a longitudinal evaluation of a horse’s adrenal function is desired.
the ACTH stimulation tests can be performed at least every 2 wk in the same horse without any risk of false negative results.
ACTH stimulation test is not a reliable tool for the diagnosis of adrenal insufficiency in horses.
